name: Trinity Commons
demographics: Trinity Commons attracts an affluent and highly educated customer base, with the surrounding 3-mile trade area showing an average household income of $131,000 and 49% of residents holding college degrees. The center draws from a dense population of over 108,000 residents within 3 miles and benefits from a strong daytime population of 140,000 workers. The proximity to Texas Christian University adds a significant student demographic of nearly 13,000, while the center's location near Amon G. Carter Stadium brings in sports fans and event attendees. The visitor profile skews toward middle to upper-middle class families and young professionals seeking quality national brands and convenient shopping experiences.
description: Trinity Commons is a premier Tom Thumb-anchored shopping center strategically located at the prominent intersection of South Hulen Street and Bellaire Drive South in Fort Worth, Texas. This 197,526 square foot community center ranks in the top 9% of comparable centers in the Dallas-Fort Worth market, drawing an impressive 3 million annual visits. The property features a strong lineup of national retailers including Ulta Beauty, DSW, Bath & Body Works, Starbucks, and Chipotle Mexican Grill, complemented by specialty services like Banfield Pet Hospital, Massage Envy, and European Wax Center. The center benefits from exceptional visibility with over 51,000 vehicles passing daily on South Hulen Street and serves an affluent trade area with average household incomes exceeding $131,000 within 3 miles. Its proximity to Texas Christian University and Amon G. Carter Stadium provides additional foot traffic from students and sports fans, while the surrounding dense residential and daytime populations ensure consistent customer engagement throughout the week.
summary: Trinity Commons is a Tom Thumb-anchored community center featuring 197,526 square feet of premier retail space with strong national tenants including Ulta Beauty, DSW, and Bath & Body Works. Located at a high-traffic Fort Worth intersection near Texas Christian University, the center ranks in the top 9% of its market and serves an affluent trade area with household incomes averaging $131,000.
